title: Sun-star Beams: Non-destructive multi-shot blending, warp tricks, and color editing in desert cave photography

summary: This Photoshop-centric craft video walks through a desert-scene post-production workflow focused on rendering a sun-star in a rock-beam composition. The presenter guides non-destructive editing, showing how to blend multiple exposures, separate sky from foreground, and improve edge lighting while preserving the sun-star. The tutorial emphasizes precise brush work, warping and alignment tools to straighten distorted rock shapes, non-destructive cloning and history-based edits, and advanced color management (Selective Color, masking, and glow) to create depth and three-dimensionality when there is little sky. It also covers common pitfalls like focus-stacking artifacts, flare, and extreme wide-angle distortion, with practical remedies including perspective warps, content-aware fixes, and versioned saves for iterative exploration.

sections.title: Sun-star emphasis and initial sky/low-area adjustments
sections.description: Early portion covers identifying a sun-star in the sky, balancing lower areas, and deciding that more sky helps showcase the star. The presenter adjusts the base shot to set up a stronger center-glow and prepares for blending in subsequent frames.

sections.title: Two-shot blending concept and sky isolation
sections.description: Discussion of taking multiple exposures or separate edits and combining them into the original frame to balance sun-star visibility with rock detail, including plans to isolate the sky for separate processing and vignette application.

sections.title: Warping and alignment to straighten rock geometry
sections.description: Demonstrates warping a tilted rock using trapezoidal perspective adjustments so the sun-star lines remain consistent. Then a duplicate/merge workflow aligns two rock shapes for a more coherent composite, with cloning to blend textures and preserve the sun-star alignment.

sections.title: Edge lighting, cloning, and local color work
sections.description: Covers edge lighting on foreground rocks with hard/soft brushes, careful feathering, and dodge/burn to sculpt light. It also introduces masking using selective color to brighten specific regions while preserving the sky and performing localized color enhancements.

sections.title: Depth and background separation; glow and background harmonization
sections.description: The presenter focuses on creating depth by intensifying beams and adding a warm glow to background elements. Techniques include selective color layering to emphasize horizon trees, adding glow under edges to simulate distance, and discussing telephoto framing when clouds are scarce.

sections.title: Advanced color control, background brightness, and warp tool overview
sections.description: Explores color consistency and background separation through de-hazing and masking, with emphasis on brightening behind the trees and using Selective Color as a mask. It also covers various warp tools (perspective, puppet) to correct distortions in wide-angle scenes for realistic shapes while noting the trade-offs in image quality.

sections.title: Wide-angle distortions, cropping, and final refinements
sections.description: Concludes with a practical note on widening perspective with Adaptive Wide Angle, selecting crop to improve composition, and applying final refinements for consistent color and brightness across light transitions.
